subject: Connectivity scope verification and pre-launch account checklist
messages:
From: Raj Malhotra <raj@helioshealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Health Network Ops <ops@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity - final scope items

Hi Markus / Grace,

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. Before we lock a cutover window we need to confirm a couple of network items so our security/compliance team can sign off: 

1) IP allowlist: we'll use the three egress ranges you provided but need a signed SLA clause that these ranges are stable during the first 30 days post-launch.
2) KMS integration: confirmation that the CMK can be imported into our AWS account and whether key rotation will require any downtime.
3) Service account roles: a minimal list of roles/redacted permissions for SRE to provision.

I attached a high-level topology and our internal intake checklist. Can you confirm these items and share the final ingress/egress CIDRs and the proposed maintenance window (we prefer 10pm–2am PT, Thu night).

Thanks,
Raj
Head of Infrastructure | Helios Health

Attachments: helios-topology.pdf, helios-intake-checklist.xlsx
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Malhotra <raj@helioshealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity - final scope items

Raj — thanks for the clear list. Below are confirmations and open items from our side: 

- IP allowlist: we confirm three egress ranges: 35.198.12.0/22, 34.120.0.0/14, 35.227.64.0/19. We can commit to keeping those stable for the first 30 days; I'll have legal send a short addendum for the SLA clause.
- KMS integration: we support importing a customer-managed key (CMK) into your AWS account. Key rotation is supported and will be non-disruptive if you enable automatic re-encrypt on our side; manual rotation will require a 5–10 minute rolling refresh during a low-traffic window.
- Service accounts: attached CSV includes the minimal roles we require for SRE: redwood-deploy, redwood-monitor-read, redwood-kms-encrypt. We will not request wide admin rights.

Proposed maintenance window: Thu 10pm–2am PT works for us. Please confirm local compliance blackout windows.

Next steps (action items):
- MARKUS: upload signed SLA addendum template by Fri EOD (I will ping legal).
- GRACE: validate that the egress ranges are acceptable for autoscaling behavior on the dedicated pool.
- NAOMI: prepare the onboarding runbook and smoke-test checklist (will attach).

I'll attach the VPC topology we use and a prelaunch connectivity checklist that maps to your intake file.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-topology-diagram.pdf, prelaunch-connectivity-checklist.xlsx
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Malhotra <raj@helioshealth.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-26T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity - final scope items

Raj — quick ops note on the egress ranges and the autoscaling behavior: 

- The three ranges Mark listed are fine from a connectivity perspective. We recommend adding the /19 range (35.227.64.0/19) to your firewall rules first, then the two /14 and /22 the day of cutover to avoid burst traffic drops.
- NAT/egress IP stability: if you want absolute IP stability during the first 30 days we can lock allocation to the dedicated pool for an extra fee; otherwise IPs are stable but subject to pooling during aggressive autoscaling events.
- Health checks & smoke tests: our runbook includes the following checks we will run during the window: token-based inference smoke (5k tokens/sec simulated), model KV cache warmup, and telemetry ingestion (1m events).

Attached is the trimmed runbook and a one-page checklist for your SREs. Ben — can you confirm the SSH jumpbox key exchange process is aligned with Helios SOC requirements?

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Program Manager, Customer Deployments | Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-accounts-and-roles.csv, runbook-smoke-tests.pdf
From: Raj Malhotra <raj@helioshealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Health Network Ops <ops@helioshealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T14:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connectivity scope verification and pre-launch account checklist

Thanks everyone — this all looks good. Confirmations from Helios: 

- SLA addendum: legal will accept the 30-day stability clause as a 30-day commitment with a follow-up review. Please send the short addendum and we'll countersign.
- Maintenance window: Thu 10pm–2am PT confirmed. We'll block the calendar and notify on-call.
- SSH key exchange: ops has a documented process and will follow the CSV roles you provided. We'll share the public keys through the secure intake link.

One outstanding ask: can Redwood provide a simple smoke-test artifact (curl script + expected JSON) we can run from our side before the window? That will speed post-cutover verification.

I'll upload the signed intake checklist after the calendar is blocked. Looking forward to the cutover.

Best,
Raj
Head of Infrastructure | Helios Health

Attachments: none
